implementationSummary: Made ranked Action Card candidates from continuous scoring (#714, B-2) durable and freshness-stamped (#715, B-3). Added a nullable ActionCard.computed_at column (models.py + additive Alembic migration 026_action_cards_computed_at, single head, down_revision=025_silver_orders_returns) carrying ScoringSignals.computed_at on a real queryable column, aligned with GoldKpiEnvelope/AnalyticsKpiEnvelope freshness semantics (ADR-038). Extended persist.py's persist_scoring_result (the existing manual-refresh persistence entry point, reused rather than forked) with a pre-upsert lookup: a card whose status is already in IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES (approved/dismissed/executing) is left completely untouched by a new candidate from re-scoring, while an 'active' or not-yet-persisted card is upserted as before via the existing (shop_id, workflow_key) unique constraint. No commit is issued inside persist_scoring_result (unchanged), so a caller's transaction rollback on failure (e.g. the Shared Compute Orchestrator's isolated scoring failure domain from #713) leaves previously-committed cards untouched with no partial write from the failed run. Did not touch shared_compute_orchestrator.py, decision_rules_scoring.py, or the material_worker/mock_analytics_reconcile call sites — those are outside the authorized path list for this domain routing; wiring persist_scoring_result onto the continuous compute scoring stage's output is called out in MODULE.md as not owned by this module and remains open (see risks).
assumptions: 'Promotion timestamp' from the issue text is satisfied by the pre-existing updated_at column (bumped on every non-suppressed upsert) plus the new computed_at column, rather than adding a dedicated surfaced_at/promoted_at column — a distinct surfacing-state column is explicitly B-4's (#716) emission-budget scope per the b-decisions.md handoff ('Pick one model in implementation... status values candidate/surfaced/suppressed or equivalent columns'), which this slice must not build.

IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES was scoped to {approved, dismissed, executing} per the issue's 'What to build' text; the AC2 bullet names only approved/executing, so dismissed-preservation is covered by a parametrized test but has no separate named AC citation.

computed_at uses DateTime(timezone=True) (matching GoldKpiEnvelope/AnalyticsKpiEnvelope) even though action_cards' other timestamp columns (approved_at, executed_at, created_at, updated_at) are naive DateTime — deliberate, since the ADR-038 alignment requirement is specifically with the envelope freshness columns, not the rest of this table.

The negative-path (AC4) test exercises real persist.py + ActionCardsRepo.upsert code via an update-path failure (not a mocked exception) because a genuine insert-path (NOT NULL constraint via a nested SAVEPOINT) failure was found not to roll back cleanly under this repo's SQLite/aiosqlite unit-test engine (no isolation_level=None + explicit BEGIN event listener is configured for it) — verified as a driver-level limitation via standalone repro scripts, not a persist.py defect.
risks: Wiring the continuous compute scoring stage (cdp_speed.decision_rules_scoring_stage / shared_compute_orchestrator.py's scoring_stage callable) to call persist_scoring_result is NOT done in this slice — that file and its call sites (services/webhook/material_worker.py, workers/tasks/mock_analytics_reconcile.py) are outside this domain's authorized paths (models.py + persist.py + database/migrations only). Until that wiring lands, persist_scoring_result is durable/idempotent/status-preserving but is not yet actually invoked from the continuous trigger in production — only from the existing manual refresh path. Flagged to Meta for correct routing of the remaining wiring task.

The AC4 negative-path test intentionally avoids exercising ActionCardsRepo's begin_nested()-savepoint insert path under failure, because that path was found unreliable to roll back under SQLite/aiosqlite in this test environment (a driver/test-fixture limitation, not observed or expected under Postgres/asyncpg in production). Production correctness of the insert-path failure/rollback is not independently verified by this slice's tests against a real Postgres engine.
